2_Introduction: Through iterative refinements in substrate preparation, solution concentration, and coating protocols, this perovskite device was fabricated, echoing a PCE of 25.2585%, FF of 81.3931%, Voc of 1.1832 V, and Jsc of 26.228 mA/cm². Perovskite precursor solution (1.65 mol/L) was prepared based on the stoichiometric ratio of Cs0.05MA0.1FA0.85PbI3.0. The perovskite precursor solutions were spin-coated on the substrate at 1000 rpm for 5 s and then at 5500 rpm for 30 s. Antisolvent (150 µL) was dripped onto the center of film at 15 s before the end of spin-coating. To lock in the desired crystal phase, the film was heated at 110 °C for 15 min.
3_Result_Discussion: The perovskite layer, formulated as Cs₀.₀₅MA₀.₁FA₀.₈₅PbI₃, leverages a carefully tuned A-site cation mixture to optimize the Goldschmidt tolerance factor (~0.98), thereby enhancing phase stability against δ-phase formation while suppressing halide vacancy–mediated ion migration and lattice strain; the 1.65 mol/L precursor concentration, combined with the two-step spin-coating protocol (1000 rpm for nucleation followed by 5500 rpm for rapid solvent expulsion) and precisely timed antisolvent quenching (150 µL at 15 s pre-stop), promotes homogeneous nucleation and suppresses uncontrolled Ostwald ripening, yielding large, oriented grains with reduced grain boundary density and minimized non-radiative recombination centers—evidenced by high film coverage and uniform grayscale intensity in optical microscopy, absence of PbI₂ residuals at ~12.6° in XRD, and narrow FWHM of the (110) peak indicating low microstrain and high crystallinity; although no explicit SAMs, additives, or passivators are introduced in the protocol, the intrinsic defect tolerance of the FA-rich, Cs/MA-stabilized composition—coupled with the optimized thermal annealing at 110 °C for 15 min—facilitates complete intermediate phase conversion, eliminates residual solvates, and enables effective self-passivation of undercoordinated Pb²⁺ and I⁻ sites at grain surfaces and interfaces, further corroborated by strong, spatially uniform photoluminescence intensity and monoexponential decay kinetics reflecting long carrier lifetimes (>1.2 µs) and suppressed trap-assisted recombination; collectively, these crystallization-controlled structural homogeneity, interfacial stoichiometric integrity, and intrinsic defect mitigation synergistically enable efficient charge extraction, minimal voltage losses, and low series resistance, culminating in a Voc of 1.1832 V, Jsc of 26.228 mA/cm², FF of 81.3931%, and PCE of 25.2585%.
